mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months is associated with falling consumer confidence and reduced labor income, which depresses discretionary spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, coupled with rising raw materials prices (proxied by RSAFS), signals input-cost inflation and supply chain stress, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months AND RSAFS > previous 12-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% in response to a financial crisis signals a liquidity trap, where traditional monetary policy loses efficacy and equity risk premia remain elevated, resulting in flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2% within one month after a major financial shock (identified ex-post by contemporaneous news)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative or flat (p > 0.10) following FEDFUNDS < 2% post-financial shock.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 4% combined with rising housing starts (HOUST) signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change > 4% AND HOUST > previous 12-month average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for six consecutive months, even as the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains unchanged, signals sticky inflation and policy lag, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4.0% for 6 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS unchanged for the same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.
